question.:question/problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y=\frac{2 x^{2}}{\ln{\left(x \right)}}$, calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=e.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
In this case, the expression for $y$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=2 x^{2}$ and $v(x)=\ln{\left(x \right)}.$

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x)&=\frac{u^{\prime}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot v^{\prime}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(2 x^{2})^{\prime}\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})-(2 x^{2})\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})^{\prime}}{(\ln{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{(4 x)\cdot (\ln{\left(x \right)})-(2 x^{2})\cdot (\frac{1}{x})}{(\ln{\left(x \right)})^{2}}\\ &=\frac{4 x \ln{\left(x \right)} - 2 x}{\ln^2 x}\\ &=\frac{2x(2\ln x-1)}{\ln^2 x}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=e$ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(e)&=\frac{2(e)(2\ln (e)-1)}{\ln^2 (e)}\\ &=\frac{2 e}{1}\\ &=2 e\end{aligned}
$$
